newsitem.title: USA: CBOT nearby soybeans end down on export data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT nearby soybeans end down on export data.

text.p: Signs that export demand for U.S. soybeans weakened helped pushed nearby CBOT contracts to a lower close Monday, traders said.
"The export inspections came in below expectations, and that triggered a wave of selling," said Victor Lespinasse, vice president with Dean Witter brokerage in Chicago.
For weeks, traders have been looking for signs that world demand for soybeans was shifting to South America as that crop is harvested and away from the United States.
So some traders said Monday's lower-than-expected export shipment figure from the U.S. Department of Agriculture showed just that.
USDA reported weekly export inspections of 8.9 million bushels, which fell well below trade expectations for ten million to 15 million bushels.
The export data had little impact on new crop soybean contracts, which caused soybean spreads to lose ground, traders said.
"The spreads are just collapsing here today (Monday)," said one floor trader.
CBOT soybeans ended 3-1/2 cents per bushel up to 7-1/4 cents down, with July down 7-1/4 cents at $8.38-1/2 a bushel.
Other factors pressuring soybeans Monday included heavy losses in soymeal futures and a sharp sell-off in wheat, traders said.
Commodity fund selling pounded soymeal futures. Most-active July fell as much as $6.20 per ton before it settled down $5.70 at $267.80.

In soybean trade on the day, Refco sold two million bushels July, Term Commodities sold one million July, ADM bought three million July and Shatkin, Arbor and Karlov bought two million July, pit traders said.
In options trading, FIMAT Futures, Inc. sold 2,300 July $8.00 puts and sold 500 July $8.25 puts. Cargill Investor Services sold 400 July $8.25 puts.
Soybean volume was estimated by CBOT at 75,000 contracts. That figure was higher than Friday's final volume of 65,464 contracts, according to CBOT data.
